b: The hotel man himself got us a car.. We went to the next place in it… There were some places to stop and see on the way..He said he'd stop too…

For breakfast we stopped at a banh mi shop and took some with us. I forgot to tell you in the last chapter.. Banh mi is hugely famous in Vietnam.. Apparently KFC, Mac and all couldn't keep up with the speed they make it.. And the shop we went to is famous worldwide.. Apparently a big chef called Anthony… they said he's a bigger shot than Gordon Ramsay himself.. They sell it with a board saying he came and praised the shop… Whenever you go, it's overflowing with people ..
The road we took was a mountain road called the Hai Van Pass… Everywhere you go is beautiful.. First we stopped at a mountain fort and enjoyed the beauty of Da Nang from above and took photos..

After that we set off, and after going a little way they stopped at a place like a lagoon.. A shallow sea without waves… a dead tree … a boat, two swings… mountains in the distance….. It looked like a place nature had carved just for taking photos… But a woman came and collected ten thousand per person for taking photos.. So then we did a photoshoot, striking all kinds of poses

Then a good sleep in the car… By the evening we'd reached Hue..We put the bags in the room and went out to look at things in the shops.. Everything terribly expensive.. So we went to a shop for dinner and ate..It was cheap and tasty…
From there we set off to see some riverside bridge.. A place like Gangaramaya… They'd lit incense and all there..There too we just sat and talked .. nothing else..just idle talk

Walking on, there were lots of street stalls… Since we couldn't spend, we just looked..There were people standing like statues.. Poor things… I don't know how they stand that long without scratching their noses… A man was playing the flute… While we enjoyed it saying it was good, Mithra alone showed off her musical learning by saying the notes were wrong.. You have to believe what she says.. She's the type who says the children singing on TV are off pitch .. off beat..
I'm someone who studied music for lack of any other option.. When I sing, it's like a donkey singing Kambhoji…I never understand this sangathi business
The next day we looked around Hue
note: The chef was probably the American food writer Anthony Bourdain, who famously praised a banh mi shop in Hoi An. Gangaramaya is a well-known Buddhist temple in Colombo. Kambhoji is a classical raga; "sangathi" means both a musical phrase and "the matter".
